subject: Renewal: multi-region terms + APAC rollout / cross-region failover
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@aureliahealth.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@aureliahealth.com
Date: Wed, 24 Feb 2027 09:14:00 -0500
Subject: Renewal questions — EU residency + APAC rollout and failover

Neha,

Quick summary: our current contract is up for renewal on 2027-04-01. We're excited to expand usage across our EU clinics and pilot in APAC, but two critical asks we've surfaced with Legal and Infrastructure:

1) EU data residency requirement for all production inference requests originating from EU regions (data-at-rest and logging)
2) APAC rollout plan with expected capacity (initial 500 concurrent sessions, scale to 2k over 6 months)
3) Cross-region failover behavior and SLAs — we need a clear failover policy that doesn't route EU-production data to non-EU storage for longer than X hours

Can you share how Redwood handles these as contract amendments and whether there's an ops runbook we can review? Ideally we want a single amendment that covers residency, capacity pricing, and failover SLAs.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Procurement, Aurelia Health
procurement@aureliahealth.com

Attachments: aurelia-network-failover-diagram.png (image, 120KB)

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 25 Feb 2027 11:27:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal questions — EU residency + APAC rollout and failover

Samir — thanks for the clear list. High level: we can cover EU residency, formalize an APAC rollout plan, and lock down a cross-region failover SLA via an amendment and an ops annex.

I've attached a working draft (redwood-sla-amendment-draft-v3.pdf) that maps to your three asks and includes two options for failover time windows (1 hour emergency fallback vs. 24 hour extended fallback). Pricing for APAC capacity is included as a committed tier + burst pricing.

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll loop in Vivek to confirm technical commit points for residency (log retention, KMS, region pinning)
- Rishi will confirm pricing bands for committed capacity and autoscale burst caps
- We can schedule a 30-min tech/contract sync later this week so Legal can sign off on the wording.

Are you available Fri 26 Feb 09:00-10:00 PT or Mon 1 Mar 14:00-15:00 PT?

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 26 Feb 2027 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Renewal questions — EU residency + APAC rollout and failover

Adding technical notes for the ops annex:

- EU residency: we can guarantee inference request bodies and logs are stored in the EU region for any EU-tagged tenant if we enable "region pinning" at account level. Key points: customer must supply a KMS in the EU or allow Redwood-managed EU KMS (option in contract). Audit logs available via the Console and can be forwarded to the customer's EU S3/GCS.

- APAC rollout: initial deployment will be provisioned in Singapore (ap-southeast-1) with a dedicated capacity pool. We can commit to 500 concurrent sessions for Q1 of the rollout, with automatic scaling policies to reach 2k within 24 weeks given committed capacity purchase (see pricing table Rishi to confirm).

- Cross-region failover: default behavior is best-effort routing to nearest healthy region. For EU production, we propose a policy:
  * Primary: EU region (eu-west-1 equivalent)
  * Short-failover: if primary unavailable, route to EU secondary in same geo (hot standby) within 60s
  * Extended-failover: if EU secondaries exhausted, route to APAC/US only after explicit customer opt-in in the annex (or during a declared emergency)

Operational requirements: DR runbooks, RTO/RPO values, and telemetry hooks will be included in the ops annex. I recommend the 60s short-failover behavior as default; the 24-hour extended fallback is negotiable for a premium and requires separate data processing addendum if customer does not opt into cross-border processing.

I'll mark up the draft with these technical clauses. Neha — please confirm whether Aurelia wants Redwood-managed KMS or will bring their own.

-Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Product — Deployments

Attachment stubs referenced: operations-runbook-template.md (internal)

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 01 Mar 2027 09:46:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Renewal questions — EU residency + APAC rollout and failover

Neha / team — pricing confirmation:

Option A (Committed):
- Base commit: 500 concurrent sessions in APAC for 12 months = $48,000/month (dedicated pool)
- Scale schedule: +250 sessions every 8 weeks up to 2,000 total (prorated)
- 10% discount if Aurelia signs 12-mo commit across both EU & APAC capacity

Option B (Burst-forward):
- No commit: on-demand pricing with higher per-token and per-session cost + guaranteed capacity reservation window of 15 mins at 1.5x token cost

Failover premium: 15% surcharge on committed capacity if customer allows extended (24h) cross-border fallback without bringing their own EU KMS.

I'll add the pricing table to the amendment draft and circulate a redline.

-Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Commercial Lead, Redwood Inference

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Renewal questions — EU residency + APAC rollout and failover

Samir — thanks for the patience. Updated summary below (short):

- EU residency: Redwood will enable account-level region pinning. Logs and inference payloads can be restricted to EU data centers. Option: customer-managed EU KMS (recommended) or Redwood-managed EU KMS (added fee).
- APAC rollout: committed 500 concurrent sessions in SG for Q1 of pilot; scale plan to 2k in 6 months. Pricing options included in the amendment.
- Failover policy: Default = hot EU standby (60s short-failover). Extended cross-border fallback to APAC/US only with explicit opt-in or in declared emergency; otherwise we will not persist EU-origin data outside EU beyond ephemeral buffering (less than 1 hour) without consent.

Action items:
1) Samir: confirm OECD-compliant DPA language and whether Aurelia will bring EU KMS or select Redwood-managed.
2) Redwood (Neha/Vivek/Rishi): finalize amendment redlines and ops annex by EOD Wed 03 Mar; we will make time for a contract+tech sync Thu 04 Mar 10:00 CET / 01:00 PT (I know that's late for us; if not workable propose alternate).

Please reply with availability for the sync and Samir please confirm the KMS preference.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
